transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on one thing. At work, I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, then a Slack ping or a color pattern—or even a siren outside—pulls me into a completely different idea before I’ve finished the line of code.
Would you say this kind of difficulty staying focused has been present since you were a child, or is this something new that started more recently?
No, this is new. It’s been going on for about three months, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase.
Over these past three months, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with needing much less sleep than usual but still feeling full of energy?

Yeah. Most days I feel really lit up, like I’m unstoppable—like Glendale finally caught up with what I’ve been building. But I also snap pretty hard when my wife or coworkers slow me down with what they call “process.”
Have you been using any drugs or stimulants—like cocaine, amphetamines, or excessive caffeine/energy drinks—more than usual during these past three months?
I’m not really sure what counts as excessive. I haven’t noticed myself using anything differently, though.
Before these past three months, have you ever gone through a period lasting two weeks or more where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember having a stretch like that, at least not one that stood out to me.
In the past three months, have you been drinking more caffeine, energy drinks, or using any other stimulants than you typically would?
I don’t think so. My caffeine use seems about the same as usual—I haven’t really noticed increasing anything.

During these past three months, have you experienced anything like hearing voices others don't hear, or holding beliefs—such as having special powers or being targeted by others—that others found unusual or not based in reality?

I haven’t been hearing voices. But I do feel pretty certain that major museums and a couple of investors are quietly watching my platform. The wording around showcases, their Instagram posts, even some emails at work—it all lines up too closely to be random.

When your wife or coworkers point out that there might be other explanations for these signs, are you able to consider that you might be wrong, or do you remain completely convinced no matter what they say?

I’ve heard what they say, but I don’t think I’m wrong. There are too many things lining up—the museum showcase wording, their Instagram posts, and even emails at work. It feels too specific to just be coincidence.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits a distinct ~3-month period of elevated/irritable mood, grandiosity, distractibility, decreased need for rest, and increased goal-directed activity, consistent with a manic episode. Accompanying this are mood-congruent grandiose/persecutory delusions (belief that museums and investors are secretly monitoring his work) that are firmly held despite reality-testing challenges, indicating psychotic features. No prior depressive episode was identified, and substance/stimulant use was explicitly denied, ruling out bipolar disorder (recurrent) and substance-induced mood disorder. The psychotic symptoms are mood-congruent and emerged concurrently with the manic symptoms, distinguishing this from a primary psychotic disorder (schizoaffective or brief psychotic disorder). This supports a diagnosis of a single manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
